goals: Explain what a vector and a matrix are in data terms
Read a dataset as a matrix of rows (samples) and columns (features)
Compute the length of a vector and the distance between two points
why: Every ML library stores data as vectors and matrices. When scikit-learn says `X` has shape (1000, 5), it means 1,000 customers described by 5 numbers each. Distances between vectors power k-NN, k-means and recommendation systems.
explain: A **vector** is just an ordered list of numbers. A flat described by (area = 900 sq ft, bedrooms = 2, age = 5 years) is the vector **[900, 2, 5]**. Each position always means the same thing.

A **matrix** is a table of numbers: a stack of vectors. In ML, each **row is one sample** (a flat, a customer, an email) and each **column is one feature**. That is exactly a spreadsheet without the headers.

Geometrically, a vector with 2 numbers is an arrow or a point on a 2D plane. With 3 numbers it is a point in 3D space. With 50 features it is a point in 50-dimensional space. You cannot picture it, but the maths works the same way.

The **length** (norm) of a vector is its distance from zero. The **distance** between two points is the length of their difference. This simple idea lets algorithms decide which customers are "similar".

formula.plain: Distance between two points = square root of the sum of the squared differences in each feature (Pythagoras, extended to many dimensions).

example.title: How similar are two customers?
example.result: A and B are 5 units apart. A customer C at [5, 3] is only √(1² + 0²) = 1 unit from A, so C is far more similar to A than B is.

mistakes: Mixing units: if one feature is in rupees (thousands) and another in years (single digits), distances are dominated by rupees. Scale features first.
Confusing rows and columns: in scikit-learn, rows are always samples.
takeaways: Vector = list of numbers = one data point
Matrix = table = whole dataset (rows = samples, columns = features)

check.q: A dataset has shape (500, 8). What does it contain?
check.why: Rows are samples and columns are features: 500 rows × 8 columns.

practice.code:
import numpy as np
a, b = np.array([4, 3]), np.array([7, 7])
print(np.linalg.norm(a - b))      # 5.0  (Euclidean distance)
X = np.array([[900, 2, 5], [1200, 3, 2]])
print(X.shape)                    # (2, 3) → 2 samples, 3 features
